name: Caledonia
summary: The last and hardest of the proving fields, an old wild country of walking trees around Caer Caledon, where Arawn's people keep the hills (30-35).

facts.text: Caledon is the battleground for levels 30 to 35 (region 250); level is the only limit in Offline DAoC.
Its central keep is Caer Caledon; an Albion, a Midgard and a Hibernia portal keep stand at the same three places as in the other battlegrounds.
Caer Caledon starts neutral in the release world.
Thidranki, Murdaigean and Caledonia were the classic battlegrounds; Abermenai came with patch 1.62 (June 2003).
Its monsters are grovewood, skulking ghouls and timber cats (levels 30-35), and Arawnite warriors, shamanesses and headhunters (31-33) in the hills of the west and north.

facts.text: Caer Caledon is held by renegades of every realm's training (armswomen and armsmen, huscarls, a hunter, a ranger, wizards, a runemaster, a guardian, all 38) under Renegade Chieftess Caledon (45), the strongest of the renegade lords; its wizards, runemaster and archers reach a long way from the walls.

facts.text: Caledonia was the Roman name for the land north of their province in Britain; 'caer' is Welsh for a fort.
Arawn is the king of Annwn, the Welsh otherworld, in the First Branch of the Mabinogi.
A Void Merchant trades realm points at the Albion portal keep; Siege Masters (50) stand at all three.

facts.text: The Historia Brittonum lists Arthur's seventh battle "in silva Caledonis, id est Cat Coit Celidon", in the Caledonian wood.

The Battle of the Trees (Cad Goddeu) was fought over a white roebuck and a whelp taken from Annwn; Arawn's champion could not be beaten until his name was guessed, and Gwydion named him Bran from the alder sprigs on his shield.
Tacitus gives the Caledonian chief Calgacus the saying that the Romans make a desert and call it peace (Agricola 30); the Irish called the painted people of the north the Cruithne.

The grovewood as Gwydion's trees waiting on the second song, Caer Caledon raised after the seventh battle, the cousins of the west, the uncut green wood and the Chieftess's roll are Living Server lore.

story:
Caledonia is the last of the fields, and the realms send their young there when they are nearly ready for the frontier.

The name is the one Rome gave the wild north, and Albion has kept it. Albion's chroniclers say Arthur fought his seventh battle in the wood of Celidon and raised Caer Caledon after it. Albion's older tellers go further back, to the battle of the trees, when Gwydion sang the wood awake to fight the host of Arawn; the grovewood, slow and rooted and angry, are those trees, still standing in their ranks. Hibernia says the painted people who held Caledonia before Rome came were cousins of the west, and that the caer was a dun before Albion renamed it. Midgard's skalds call it the grey country, and teach their young never to cut green wood there.

Arawn's people still keep the hills of the west and north: warriors along the western ridges, shamanesses at the old barrows, headhunters in the far north. Skulking ghouls dig at the barrows and timber cats hunt between the trees. Caer Caledon itself is held by the strongest renegades of the four fields, soldiers of every realm's training under a chieftess who has taken its name, and its walls reach a long way.

Every soldier who leaves Caledonia goes on to the frontier, and none of them is ever let back in.
legend: Caledonia is the 30-35 battleground, the last before the frontier. Caer Caledon in the middle is the hardest renegade keep of the four: armsmen, armswomen, huscarls, wizards, a runemaster, a hunter and a ranger, all level 38, under Renegade Chieftess Caledon at 45, and the casters and archers have long aggro range, so you get shot well before you reach the walls. Bring a full group, siege gear from the Siege Masters at your portal keep and healers who can keep up. The Arawnite warriors line the western hills and their headhunters sit in the far north; grovewood, timber cats and skulking ghouls are everywhere and aggro. There is a Void Merchant at the Albion portal keep. Players call it Cale and say the renegades there are tougher than real players.

loremaster.intro: Caledonia, the last of the proving fields. Ask me of [Caer Caledon] and its [Chieftess], of the [grovewood], or of the [Arawnites] in the hills.

topics.caer caledon: A caer of old stone at the heart of the field, held by the strongest renegades of the four: armsmen and armswomen, huscarls, wizards, a runemaster, a hunter and a ranger, under the [Chieftess]. Its casters and archers reach a long way from the walls.
topics.chieftess: Renegade Chieftess Caledon, who keeps the caer and has taken its name, as the renegade chieftains of the fields do. Every realm says she was one of its own once. She has never said which.
topics.grovewood: The walking trees of Caledonia, slow, rooted and angry. They stand in ranks facing the western hills, and they strike at whatever comes among them.
topics.arawnites: The people of Arawn, who keep Caledonia's western and northern hills: warriors in a line along the west, shamanesses at the barrows, headhunters in the far north. Albion's Church preaches against them by name. They call the skulking ghouls at the barrows their lord's dogs, and leave them be.

book.title: The Chieftess's Roll, kept by a scribe of Caer Caledon
pages: I keep the roll for the Chieftess, since no realm keeps one for us. We are deserters. I was a scribe of Albion's muster at Castle Sauvage and walked away from it; the woman on the wall beside me was a huscarl of Midgard who walked away from hers, and the ranger at the north gate was a Hibernian of the Path. We hold Caer Caledon because it was empty and old and nobody's. The fields let us in though we are grown. There are three explanations of that in three realms, and they come to the same thing: we belong to nobody, and the fields do not count us.

The country is older than any of us. The trees stand in ranks facing the western hills, and they do not like axes; we cut nothing green. The painted people in those hills pray to the king under the hills and call the ghouls at the barrows his dogs, and leave them be. So do we. The painted people do not trouble the caer. They trouble the young who come up from the portal keeps, and the young trouble us, and that is the order of things in Caledonia.

The young come up the slope at us every summer, and we hold the walls, and they fall, and in the morning they are back at their gates and we are where we were. The Chieftess watches them come from the gatehouse. She says they are the best of their realms, and that within the year they will be at the frontier. I asked her once why she takes such care over the walls against children. She said someone has to teach them that a wall can be held, and she would rather it were someone who wished them well.

albion.story: Albion tells Caledonia as its own oldest wild. Rome named it, Arthur fought his seventh battle in its wood and raised Caer Caledon after, and before either, Gwydion sang its trees awake to fight the host of Arawn. Albion's squires are told that the grovewood are older than the realm and owe it nothing, and that the people in the hills are Arawn's, whom the Church names from the pulpit. They are told the rest of it by the storytellers, if they ask.

loremaster.intro: Caledonia is the last of the proving fields, and the name is the one Rome gave the wild north, which Albion has kept. Arthur fought his seventh battle in the wood of Celidon and raised [Caer Caledon] after it. The trees that walk there, the [grovewood], are older than Arthur's war; they are what is left of the [battle of the trees]. The hills belong to the [Arawnites], who belong to Arawn.

topics.battle of the trees: When a man of Gwynedd stole a white roebuck and a hound out of Annwn, Arawn came up out of the earth with a host to take them back, and Gwydion, who had no host, went into the wood of Celidon and sang the trees into one. They came down the hill in ranks, the alders first and the oak last, and they fought all day, and the day was won when Gwydion read the name of Arawn's champion in the sprigs on his shield. That is the whole of the matter as the old books give it. They do not say that anyone ever sang the trees back to sleep, and the grovewood are standing in their ranks yet.

hibernia.story: Hibernia tells Caledonia as a country of cousins. The painted people who held the wild north before Rome came were the Cruithne, and the filidh say they went over the sea out of Hibernia and took the north for themselves, and that the caer in the middle was a dun of theirs before Albion put a new word on it. The Hibernian young who go to Caledonia are told that they are going to a place their own people held, and that the trees there are nobody's cousins.

loremaster.intro: Caledonia, the last of the proving fields, and the Albions will tell you it's theirs because the Romans named it. Before ever a Roman saw it, the painted people held it, and they were [cousins of the west]. The caer in the middle, [Caer Caledon], was a dun first. The [grovewood] walk there and the [Arawnites] keep the hills, and neither of them is anybody's cousin.

topics.cousins of the west: The painted people of the north were the Cruithne, and our filidh say they went over the sea out of Hibernia in the old days and took the wild north for themselves, and painted themselves for war, and fought the Romans to a standstill under a chief who told his men that the Romans make a desert and call it peace. The Albions have that speech in a Roman book, and they're very proud of having it. They never seem to notice whose side it was spoken on.

midgard.story: Midgard's skalds call Caledonia the grey country and say that the grovewood are a host that was never stood down. Midgard's young are told one thing before they go there, and every one of them keeps it: cut no green wood in Caledonia. The skalds count the renegades of Caer Caledon as warriors who chose their own jarl, and say that the huscarls on its walls are the best fighters in any field, which some of them say with envy.

loremaster.intro: Caledonia. The skalds call it the grey country, the last of the proving fields and the hardest. The [grovewood] are a host that was never stood down, so we cut no [green wood] there. The [Arawnites] keep the hills. [Caer Caledon] is held by renegades, and its [Chieftess] has warriors of ours on her walls.

topics.green wood: A youth of Midgard going to Caledonia is told one thing by his elders: cut no green wood. The skalds say the grovewood are a host that was never stood down, and that a host remembers. Every youth of Midgard has kept the rule, so far as anyone knows, and the grovewood kill them anyway, which the skalds say only shows how much worse it would be otherwise.
